A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 21-page versions of the same paper. Text comparison and page rendering support reliable comparison of the main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.9.

before.justification: v2 reports original activation-geometry experiments across four LLMs and four dataset families, plus probe evaluations and steering interventions in Appendices A.4 and A.9.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical results, including geometric measurements, relevant-versus-random context comparisons, probe accuracies, and steering label-switching rates.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same four-prompt procedure, residual-stream extraction, truth-vector construction, and geometric measurements. The appendix probing and steering procedures are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DRUID subsets, MF2, ConflictQA counter-memory and parametric conditions, and LegalBench Corporate Lobbying variants. Context scenarios and task coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: The five random-context controls and evaluated model set are unchanged. Appendix A.4 retains the same logistic regression, linear SVM, mass-mean, and MLP probe comparisons.

E3.justification: Both retain identical model configurations, greedy decoding, instruction-following filtering, context-length controls, geometric metrics, and 80/20 train-test splits for probing and steering.

E4.justification: The random-context comparisons, asymmetric-context magnitude analysis, probing, output-probability correlations, instruction-following analysis, and steering interventions are retained without revision.

E5.justification: Wilcoxon signed-rank testing, Bonferroni corrections with 160 or 320 tests, and standard-error reporting in Figures 11–12 are identical. No run-count or seed information changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results, significance markings, and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, including Tables 2–12, probe accuracies, probability correlations, and steering outcomes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–13 are identical. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about layer-dependent directional changes, increased truth-vector magnitude, and sensitivity to context relevance.

C2.justification: The interpretations of model-size differences, knowledge conflict, legal-context difficulty, and practical implications are unchanged. Section 7 and the appendix retain the same limitations and qualifications.

D1.justification: Implementation and preprocessing descriptions, model specifications, A100/H100 hardware disclosure, approximately 500 GPU hours, and the code-access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, research positioning, and cited works are unchanged. The LegalBench reference crosses a different page boundary in v3 but retains the same bibliographic content.

P1.justification: Section 9 adds thanks to Theresia Veronika Rampisela and Pietro Tropeano, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining wording and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded acknowledgement causes minor bibliography reflow across columns and pages 10–11. All figures and tables retain their content, design, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 adds named acknowledgements and updates the version stamp, with minor bibliography reflow. Scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain identical, so overall paper quality does not meaningfully change.
